Reflect on the patterns that are resurfacing without turning every feeling into a verdict.
sun_corpus.close: Come home to yourself. Let care include you.

sun_corpus.tldrWhat: The Sun in Virgo puts daily systems, work, health, service, and the small choices that keep life functioning under review.
sun_corpus.tldrTakeaway: The details matter, but not all equally. Practice discernment.
sun_corpus.opening: Welcome to Virgo season’s reality check. This is the month to recognize which systems actually support you and which ones are just daily punishment disguised as productivity. A routine is not useful because it looks disciplined; it is useful because it helps your life work.
sun_corpus.tension: Your wellness routine can become another way to fail. Some habits look like discipline from the outside but are just outdated agreements you forgot to renegotiate. Virgo’s attention to detail becomes exhausting when every imperfection turns into another task and every act of care becomes another standard to meet.
sun_corpus.development: Virgo’s deeper teaching is that the sacred lives in the mundane. Tending to the small things is how you heal the whole, but the small things still have to support you. Start with one system that feels more like a task than support. Pick one. Just one. Fix the repeat problem before you add another routine on top of it.
sun_corpus.close: Create one simple, sustainable practice you can maintain even on your worst days.

sun_corpus.tldrWhat: The Sun in Libra brings relationships, fairness, compromise, boundaries, and the exchange between people into focus.
sun_corpus.tldrTakeaway: True balance isn’t about everyone being happy. It’s about honest assessment of who’s been carrying the weight.
sun_corpus.opening: Balance is a moment, not a state. It’s a pause in constant motion, not a destination you arrive at. The scales are supposed to move; that is how they measure actual weight, actual worth, and actual balance.
sun_corpus.tension: Libra wants harmony, but harmony without authenticity is just performance. Some conflicts are worth having because they lead to deeper understanding. If the arrangement only works when one person stays agreeable, gives in first, or makes themselves easier to live with, the problem is not the conflict.
sun_corpus.development: Look at who keeps adjusting, who gets accommodated, and who has been doing the work of keeping the peace. Healthy boundaries can create more intimacy, not less, because the relationship finally has two people in it instead of one person managing the comfort of both. The goal is not a perfectly still scale. It is an exchange that can keep recalibrating as people and circumstances change.
sun_corpus.close: Practice showing up as yourself in your relationships. This season teaches you the difference between keeping the peace and creating it.

sun_corpus.tldrWhat: The Sun in Scorpio brings endings, intimacy, shared resources, power, and what has been kept below the surface into focus.
sun_corpus.tldrTakeaway: Scorpio doesn’t kill what’s alive. It names what’s already dead and asks why you’re still propping it up.
sun_corpus.opening: Here’s what Scorpio does: composting. Death, decay, the necessary rot that feeds new growth. Every year when the Sun enters Scorpio, we’re asked to identify what is already decomposing, even when the structure around it is still standing.
sun_corpus.tension: A relationship can end emotionally months before it ends logistically. A career can stop feeding you while you keep showing up. An identity can survive because you have been performing it out of habit. Scorpio makes the cost of preserving what has already ended much harder to ignore.
sun_corpus.development: Taurus wants peace, but Scorpio knows that peace can come after the confrontation, not instead of it. Shared money, intimacy, support, resentment, control, and the help you will not ask for can all show you where the deeper exchange has become stuck. The point is not to manufacture a crisis. It is to stop using familiarity as proof that something is still alive.
sun_corpus.close: Transformation isn’t the breakdown, refusing it will be.

sun_corpus.tldrWhat: The Sun in Sagittarius turns attention toward truth, belief, meaning, perspective, and the story you are using to choose a direction.
sun_corpus.tldrTakeaway: What do you know versus what do you believe?
sun_corpus.opening: Sagittarius is the sign of storytellers and philosophers. This season turns your attention to the stories that have come to define your life, especially the ones you have already outgrown. A story can give your life meaning for years and still stop fitting the person who is living it now.
sun_corpus.tension: Gemini asks, “What do I know right now?” Sagittarius replies, “But what does it mean in the bigger picture?” That larger view is useful until belief becomes more important than the facts that complicate it. Optimism can keep you moving, but it can also keep you loyal to a direction that no longer makes sense.
sun_corpus.development: What do you still claim to believe, and does your life reflect that belief? Travel, study, philosophy, teaching, religion, and unfamiliar perspectives can widen the frame, but expansion matters most when it changes how you live. Now is the time to reclaim authorship, speak the truth you have been editing out, and let go of the narratives that keep shrinking what you think is possible.
sun_corpus.close: Choose meaning. Choose direction. Choose yourself.

sun_corpus.tldrWhat: The Sun in Capricorn brings responsibility, time, ambition, authority, and the structure underneath long-term goals into focus.
sun_corpus.tldrTakeaway: What legacy do you want to create, and what will it actually require from you?
sun_corpus.opening: Capricorn season brings accountability and pragmatism. This is a season of growth through action, where maturity means embracing responsibility and confronting the truth of where you stand. A goal changes once the time, money, limits, and consequences attached to it become part of the conversation.
sun_corpus.tension: With responsibility comes doubt. Look closely at what the doubt is pointing to before you dismiss it as fear. Sometimes it is showing you the weak part of the plan, the missing resource, or the responsibility nobody has accounted for. Ambition gets more expensive when responsibility keeps landing on the same person.
sun_corpus.development: Capricorn asks you to think beyond the immediate win. What can the structure support one year from now, five years from now, or ten? What needs to be redistributed, clarified, funded, or ended for the goal to remain worth pursuing? Long-term success is not just reaching the destination; it is building something that does not require you to sacrifice the rest of your life to keep it standing.
sun_corpus.close: Build the structure that can support the life around the goal.

sun_corpus.tldrWhat: The Sun in Aquarius brings community, systems, individuality, collective responsibility, and the future we are building together into focus.
sun_corpus.tldrTakeaway: Who do you stand with, and what do you stand for?
sun_corpus.opening: The Sun in Aquarius illuminates the liminal space between what has been and what could be. This is the season to think big, dream wide, and build bridges that connect us to a better tomorrow. The future stops being abstract when your values begin changing how you participate in the present.
sun_corpus.tension: Aquarius season reveals which friendships and communities honor your individuality while connecting you to something greater. Seeing what is wrong with a system is not the same as changing it, and standing outside the group can protect independent thought while also making it easier to avoid responsibility for what happens inside it.
sun_corpus.development: Aquarius asks us to commit to a vision and to the ideals that shape our communities and the future we are building together. Its traditional Saturn rulership gives the sign a serious relationship to systems and collective responsibility; its modern association with Uranus adds disruption and experimentation. The useful question is not how different you can be. It is what your difference makes possible for other people.
sun_corpus.close: Build the bridge between who you’ve been and who you’re becoming, then bring something useful back to the collective.

sun_corpus.tldrWhat: The Sun in Pisces brings endings, surrender, intuition, imagination, grief, and the space between one cycle and the next into focus.
sun_corpus.tldrTakeaway: This is the final tide before Aries season. Let it take what no longer belongs.
sun_corpus.opening: Pisces is the last sign. The end of the road, and the space between endings and beginnings. This season asks you to stay with what is dissolving long enough to understand what you are no longer meant to carry into the next cycle.
sun_corpus.tension: Not all dreams are meant to last. Some dissolve and leave only the lesson behind. Pisces can blur the line between intuition and longing, compassion and self-erasure, surrender and avoidance, which is why forcing a clean answer can create more confusion than giving the situation time to reveal what is actually there.
sun_corpus.development: Not everything can be thought through. Some paths require feeling, intuition, and surrender to the unknown. Give unfinished feelings, grief, old dreams, and the parts of your life that do not resolve on command enough room to move. If something is ending, you do not need to invent the next chapter before you are ready to close this one.
sun_corpus.close: Let what is ending finish. The next cycle does not need to carry everything this one could not resolve.

Pisces can blur the line between intuition and longing, compassion and self-erasure, surrender and avoidance, which is why forcing a clean answer can create more confusion than giving the situation time to reveal what is actually there.

Not everything can be thought through. Some paths require feeling, intuition, and surrender to the unknown. Give unfinished feelings, grief, old dreams, and the parts of your life that do not resolve on command enough room to move. If something is ending, you do not need to invent the next chapter before you are ready to close this one.

Let what is ending finish. The next cycle does not need to carry everything this one could not resolve.

seasonal_context.copy: The March equinox begins spring in the Northern Hemisphere. Day and night briefly meet at equal length before the days continue growing longer. Aries Season begins at the same moment, opening the zodiac year with the first spark of a new cycle.

The March equinox begins autumn in the Southern Hemisphere. Day and night briefly meet at equal length before the nights continue growing longer. Aries Season begins at the same moment, opening the zodiac year even as the physical season turns toward autumn.
The Sun enters Aries at the March equinox, when day and night briefly meet at equal length across the globe. Aries begins the zodiac year at this turning point of the solar cycle.
The Summer Solstice marks the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere, a turning point where light peaks, then slowly begins its descent. The Sun enters Cancer at the same moment.
The June Solstice marks the shortest day of the year in the Southern Hemisphere. Darkness reaches its peak and the light slowly begins to return as the Sun enters Cancer.
The Sun enters Cancer at the June solstice, one of the four turning points of the solar year. The balance of light changes direction across the globe as Cancer Season begins.

The September equinox begins autumn in the Northern Hemisphere. Day and night are equal for approximately one moment, then darkness begins to overtake light. Libra Season begins at the same turning point.

The September equinox begins spring in the Southern Hemisphere. Day and night are equal for approximately one moment, then light continues to overtake darkness. Libra Season begins at the same turning point.
The Sun enters Libra at the September equinox, when day and night are equal for approximately one moment before the balance shifts again.
The Winter Solstice marks the darkest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere, a time of stillness and reflection. From here the light slowly begins to return as Capricorn Season begins.
The December Solstice marks the longest day of the year in the Southern Hemisphere. From here the light slowly begins to recede as Capricorn Season begins.
The Sun enters Capricorn at the December solstice, one of the four turning points of the solar year. The balance of light changes direction across the globe as Capricorn Season begins.
